test_title: SSC GD Constable Previous Year Paper (Held on: 14th December 2021 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: If V and S denote the volume and Total Surface Area of a cuboid (of sides a, b, c), respectively, then which of the following is true?
solution:
**Given:**

V and S denote the volume and Total Surface Area of a cuboid

Sides a, b, c

**Concept used:**

Volume of a cuboid = l × b × h

Total surface area = 2(lb + bh + lh)

Here, l = length, b = breadth, h = height

**Calculation:**

V = (a × b × c)

S = 2(ab + bc + ac)

Now,

From options:

Option 1:

(1)/((a × b× c)) = (2)/(2(ab + bc + ac)) × (a + b + c)

⇒ (1)/((a × b× c)) = ((a + b + c))/((ab + bc + ac))

Not satisfying

Option 2:

(1)/((a × b× c)) = 2(ab + bc + ac)((1)/(a)+(1)/(b)+(1)/(c))

⇒ (1)/((a × b× c)) = 2(ab + bc + ac)((ab+bc+ac)/(a× b× c))

⇒ (1)/((a × b× c)) = (2(ab + bc + ac)²)/((a× b× c))

Not satisfying

Option 3:

(1)/((a × b× c)) = (2)/(2(ab + bc + ac)) × ((1)/(a)+(1)/(b)+(1)/(c))

⇒ (1)/((a × b× c)) = (1)/((ab + bc + ac))((ab+bc+ac)/(a× b× c))

⇒ (1)/((a × b× c)) = (1)/((a× b× c))

Satisfying

Option 4:

{(a × b× c)} = (2)/(2(ab + bc + ac)) × ((1)/(a)+(1)/(b)+(1)/(c))

⇒ {(a × b× c)} = (1)/((ab + bc + ac))((ab+bc+ac)/(a× b× c))

⇒ {(a × b× c)} = (1)/((a× b× c))

Not satisfying

**∴ Required answer is Option 3.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] __Alternate Method__** 

V = abc

S = 2(ab+ bc +ca)

Hence, a = V/bc, b = V/ac, c = V/ab

S = 2(V/c + V/a + V/b)

S = 2V(1/a + 1/b + 1/c)

or (1/V) = (2/S) (1/a + 1/b + 1/c)
